---
title: "ICB Case Finder"
output: html_document
---

Purpose: find illustrative ICB crisis cases that fit specific hypothesis
profiles (e.g. "a democratic intervener with ties to both sides that
succeeded"), and verify that the match is genuine -- i.e. that the SAME
intervener satisfies all the conditions, rather than different conditions
being satisfied by different interveners within the same crisis (which the
crisis-dyad-level aggregated variables in `matched_caliper` cannot
distinguish, since `regime_type_int`, `ties_to_both_sides`, etc. are each
built with `any()` across all interveners independently).

```{r, echo = F, message = F}
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(knitr)
```

## Step 1: load the crisis-dyad level matched sample

```{r}
load(here("models", "ICB_models.RData"))
# brings in matched_caliper and all h1.x_*/h2.x_* model objects
```

## Step 2: build (or load cached) intervener-row-level data

`matched_caliper` is aggregated to one row per crisis-dyad, with
intervener characteristics (`regime_type_int`, `ties_to_both_sides`,
`military_expenditure_int`, `state_capacity_int`, ...) collapsed across
potentially several interveners via `any()`/`mean()`. To check whether a
single intervener actually satisfies a combination of conditions, we need
the pre-aggregation table with one row per (crisis-dyad x intervener).

That table is `ICBdy_step16` inside `ICB Cleaning.Rmd` (built right before
the final `group_by(crdynum) %>% summarise(...)` step, and after military
interveners -- `intervener_category_id == 5` -- are excluded, matching how
`regime_type_int`/`ties_to_both_sides`/etc. in `matched_caliper` are
constructed). Rebuilding it means re-running most of the cleaning
pipeline (it needs the large V-Dem file), so we cache the result and only
rebuild when the cache is missing.

```{r}
step16_cache_path <- here("Cleaned Data", "ICBdy_step16.rds")

if (!file.exists(step16_cache_path)) {

  purled_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
  knitr::purl(
    here("R Code", "ICB Cleaning.Rmd"),
    output = purled_path,
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  lines <- readLines(purled_path)
  stop_line <- grep("ICBdy_step16\\s*=", lines)[1]

  if (is.na(stop_line)) {
    stop(
      "Could not find the line that builds ICBdy_step16 in ",
      "'ICB Cleaning.Rmd' -- the cleaning script structure may have ",
      "changed. Update the search pattern above."
    )
  }

  writeLines(lines[1:stop_line], purled_path)
  source(purled_path)

  saveRDS(ICBdy_step16, step16_cache_path)

} else {

  ICBdy_step16 <- readRDS(step16_cache_path)

}

cat("ICBdy_step16: one row per (crisis-dyad x non-military intervener)\n")
cat("nrow =", nrow(ICBdy_step16), "\n")
```

If you edit `ICB Cleaning.Rmd` (e.g. add/change variables upstream of
`ICBdy_step16`), delete `Cleaned Data/ICBdy_step16.rds` so this rebuilds.

## Step 3: generic case-finding function

`find_cases()` takes:

- `agg_filter`: a filter expression evaluated on `matched_caliper`
  (crisis-dyad level) -- this is the "does the aggregate story look right"
  pass.
- `intervener_filter`: a filter expression evaluated on `ICBdy_step16`
  (intervener level) -- this is the "is there a single intervener that
  actually satisfies all the conditions" pass.

It returns one row per crisis-dyad matched by `agg_filter`, flagged
`genuine_match = TRUE` only if at least one individual intervener in that
crisis-dyad also satisfies `intervener_filter`, with that intervener's
name(s) attached. Rows with `genuine_match = FALSE` are crisis-dyads where
the aggregated variables in `matched_caliper` look like they fit the
story, but no single intervener actually does -- these should be treated
as false positives, not cited as examples.

```{r}
find_cases <- function(agg_filter, intervener_filter, extra_cols = character(0)) {

  agg_filter <- rlang::enquo(agg_filter)
  intervener_filter <- rlang::enquo(intervener_filter)

  cases <- matched_caliper %>%
    filter(!!agg_filter) %>%
    select(
      crdynum, crisno, crisname, namea, nameb, trgyrdy,
      regime_type_int, ties_to_both_sides, forout, outesr,
      military_expenditure_int, state_capacity_int,
      all_of(extra_cols)
    )

  matching_interveners <- ICBdy_step16 %>%
    filter(crdynum %in% cases$crdynum, !!intervener_filter) %>%
    group_by(crdynum) %>%
    summarise(
      matching_interveners = paste(unique(actor), collapse = "; "),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  cases %>%
    left_join(matching_interveners, by = "crdynum") %>%
    mutate(genuine_match = !is.na(matching_interveners))
}


# for diagnosing a FALSE case: show every intervener in that crisis-dyad
# and which of the two conditions (if any) each one individually satisfies
show_roster <- function(cd) {
  ICBdy_step16 %>%
    filter(crdynum == cd) %>%
    select(
      actor, intervener_category, regime_type_int,
      ties_to_both_sides, state_capacity_int, military_expenditure_int
    ) %>%
    as.data.frame()
}
```

## Step 4: the two requested case types

Type 1: a democratic intervener with ties to both sides, that succeeded
at making peace (long-term tension reduction).

Type 2: a weak democratic intervener that struggled to make peace
(short-term failure to reach agreement). "Weak" is defined on
`state_capacity_int` (CINC, a share of world capability normalized every
year) rather than `military_expenditure_int` (raw nominal $, trends up
over the 20th century and isn't comparable across eras -- see the bottom
of this file for the check).

```{r}
cap_q25 <- quantile(
  matched_caliper$state_capacity_int,
  probs = 0.25,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

case_type1 <- find_cases(
  agg_filter = regime_type_int == 1 & ties_to_both_sides == 1 & outesr == 1,
  intervener_filter = regime_type_int == 1 & ties_to_both_sides == 1
)

case_type2 <- find_cases(
  agg_filter = regime_type_int == 1 &
    state_capacity_int <= cap_q25 & forout == 0,
  intervener_filter = regime_type_int == 1 & state_capacity_int <= cap_q25
)

cat("Type 1: genuine matches =", sum(case_type1$genuine_match),
    "/", nrow(case_type1), "\n")
cat("Type 2: genuine matches =", sum(case_type2$genuine_match),
    "/", nrow(case_type2), "\n")

case_type1 %>%
  select(crdynum, crisno, crisname, namea, nameb, trgyrdy,
         genuine_match, matching_interveners) %>%
  as.data.frame()

case_type2 %>%
  select(crdynum, crisno, crisname, namea, nameb, trgyrdy,
         genuine_match, matching_interveners) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

To inspect why a specific crisis-dyad is NOT a genuine match, pull its
`crdynum` from the tables above and run e.g. `show_roster(476)`.

## Step 5: save results

```{r}
dir.create(here("Case Examples"), showWarnings = FALSE)

final <- bind_rows(
  case_type1 %>%
    mutate(type = "Type1_democratic_ties_longterm_success") %>%
    select(type, crdynum, crisno, crisname, namea, nameb, trgyrdy,
           genuine_match, matching_interveners),
  case_type2 %>%
    mutate(type = "Type2_weak_democratic_shortterm_failure") %>%
    select(type, crdynum, crisno, crisname, namea, nameb, trgyrdy,
           genuine_match, matching_interveners)
)

write.csv(
  final,
  here("Case Examples", "case_summary_with_interveners.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Appendix: why `state_capacity_int` (CINC) instead of `military_expenditure_int`

`military_expenditure_int` is nominal (not inflation- or era-adjusted),
so pooling it across ~1920-2000 and taking a flat quantile mostly just
picks out early-20th-century cases (global nominal military budgets were
far smaller back then). `state_capacity_int` (the NMC CINC score) is a
share of that year's world total, so it's comparable across eras.

```{r}
cat("correlation with year, military_expenditure_int:",
    cor(matched_caliper$military_expenditure_int, matched_caliper$trgyrdy,
        use = "complete.obs"), "\n")
cat("correlation with year, state_capacity_int (CINC):",
    cor(matched_caliper$state_capacity_int, matched_caliper$trgyrdy,
        use = "complete.obs"), "\n")
```
